shorts.title: Brontosaurus Wore Somebody Else's Head for 47 Years
shorts.outro: Then Doug went back to meet the real one, holding the 1932 drawing. He went looking for the boxy head. Full video below.
shorts.description: Marsh gave his headless skeleton a borrowed boxy skull from a different animal, and the Carnegie Museum's Apatosaurus wore a Camarasaurus head for 47 years, from 1932 until the swap in 1979; see what Doug found when he went to meet the real one in the full episode.

shorts.title: Dimetrodon Is More Closely Related to You Than to T. Rex
shorts.outro: Doug brought a family photo to say hello. His cap ended up somewhere very specific. Full video below.
shorts.end_card: WHERE DID DOUG'S CAP END UP?
shorts.description: Dimetrodon lived about three times further from Tyrannosaurus in time than Tyrannosaurus lives from you, grew steak-knife teeth 40 million years before meat-eating dinosaurs did, and sits on the branch that led to mammals; find out where Doug's cap ended up in the full episode.

shorts.title: Scientists Still Can't Agree What Spinosaurus Looked Like
shorts.hook: Spinosaurus is fifteen meters long, and nobody agrees what it looked like.
shorts.outro: Behind Doug, something that matched none of the four cards rose out of the river. Full video below.
shorts.description: In 2022 one study argued the 15-meter Spinosaurus dove underwater for its food and another argued it was too buoyant to dive and waded the shallows on two legs; see which Spinosaurus came out of the river for Doug in the full episode.
